```{r}
#| message: false
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
```

# Exercise 1: Fun with trig

```{r}
xx <- seq(-pi, 2*pi, length.out = 234)

data.frame(
  x          = xx,
  `sin(x)`   = sin(xx),
  `sin(x)^2` = sin(xx)^2,
  `sin(x^2)` = sin(xx^2),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  pivot_longer(-x, names_to = "fun", values_to = "y") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, color = fun)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Angle (rad.)", y = "y = f(x)", color = NULL)
```

# Exercise 2: More fun with trig

```{r}
data.frame(
  x              = xx,
  `sin(cos(x))`  = sin(cos(xx)),
  `cos(sin(x))`  = cos(sin(xx)),
  `cos(x)`       = cos(xx),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  pivot_longer(-x, names_to = "fun", values_to = "y") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, color = fun)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Angle (rad.)", y = "y = f(x)", color = NULL)
```

# Exercise 3: Resolution and tan

```{r}
# Plot tan(x) at three resolutions to see how point density affects appearance
res_levels <- 10^(2:4)   # 100, 1000, 10000 points

df_tan <- lapply(res_levels, function(n) {
  x <- seq(0, 2*pi, length.out = n)
  data.frame(x = x, y = tan(x), n_pts = paste(n, "pts"))
}) |>
  bind_rows()

ggplot(df_tan, aes(x = x, y = y, color = n_pts)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-50, 50)) +
  labs(x = "Angle (rad.)", y = "y = f(x)",
       title = "tan(x) at different resolutions", color = NULL)
```
